title: Grain, surrogate keys and bridge tables

videos.script: Three mistakes in a warehouse produce numbers that look right and are not. This lesson is one for each. {{three}} The first is the grain. Ana adds the shipping fee to the sales table, and the shop's freight bill grows by a hundred thousand reais that nobody paid. {{grain}} The second is the keys. A customer changes their e-mail. A system is replaced and starts counting from one again. A sale has no customer at all. Each of those, joined the obvious way, loses rows or attaches them to the wrong person. {{keys}} The third is a book with three authors. Ask for revenue by author, add it up, and the shop has sold sixteen million reais more than it ever took. {{authors}} None of these raises an error. Every one of them returns a table of plausible numbers. {{plausible}} So for each one, Ana first makes the mistake on purpose, measures how far off it is, and then builds the repair: a grain written down, a key the warehouse owns, a row for the unknown, and a table with a weight in it. {{repair}}
